title: Self-Help Ghouls Are Charging People Absurd Prices to Talk to Impersonator Chatbots
titleZh: 新的生意：贩卖数字化的自己
summary:
尽管专家和专业人士并不推荐，仍有数百万人通过人工智能聊天机器人寻求情感支持与建议。这些人大多身处人生低谷，可能也无力自行负担他们真正需要的专业帮助与支持。自助产业显然注意到了这一趋势，看到了这群正在寻找援助的人，继而形成了一种行业共识：“也许，我们可以从他们身上赚到钱。”

来源：Gizmodo；作者：AJ Dellinger；原文发布时间：2026-01-16 20:00:00

paragraphs.contentEn: Against the recommendations of experts and professionals, millions of people use AI chatbots for emotional support and advice. These are often people who are in vulnerable times in their lives, perhaps unable to pay out of pocket for the type of help and support they need. The self-help industry is apparently aware of this trend, has seen this demographic of people in search of help, and collectively said, “You know, we can probably make some cash off these people.”
paragraphs.contentZh: 尽管专家和专业人士并不推荐，仍有数百万人通过人工智能聊天机器人寻求情感支持与建议。这些人大多身处人生低谷，可能也无力自行负担他们真正需要的专业帮助与支持。自助产业显然注意到了这一趋势，看到了这群正在寻找援助的人，继而形成了一种行业共识：“也许，我们可以从他们身上赚到钱。”

paragraphs.contentEn: The Wall Street Journal reports that there is a trend of gurus creating chatbots that replicate their style and voice, allowing people to “talk” to an AI-powered recreation of them to get “personalized” advice in the style of their life coach of choice. The bots are loaded up with all of the experts’ books, lectures, and interviews, and can spit out answers to questions in the style of the author. All you have to do is pay a monthly subscription to access it all.
paragraphs.contentZh: 据《华尔街日报》报道，目前兴起了一种新趋势，一些导师型人物正在打造能够复刻自身言行风格的聊天机器人，用户可以通过与这些人工智能驱动的数字分身“对话”，像和自己心仪的人生导师交流一样，获取所谓的“个性化”建议。这些机器人学习了相关专家的全部著作、演讲和访谈内容，能够以专家本人的风格进行应答。用户只需支付月度订阅费，即可使用全部功能。

paragraphs.contentEn: How much it’ll cost you depends on the expert. Per WSJ, dating coach Matthew Hussey charges people $39 per month for “Matthew AI,” which has reportedly already had over one million conversations, and users have spent 1.9 million minutes talking to it via voice chat. Tony Robbins will hit you for $99 per month for his life coach bot—but you can get started with an introductory rate of $0.99 for the first 14 days! Spiritual teacher David Ghiyam offers a sliding scale option so people can talk to an AI version of him for just $1 per month, which certainly beats paying his private coaching rate of $15,000 per hour.
paragraphs.contentZh: 具体费用取决于你所选择的专家。据《华尔街日报》报道，情感导师马修·赫西推出的聊天机器人“Matthew AI”月费为39美元，据称该机器人已累计产生超过100万次对话，用户通过语音聊天与其互动的总时长达到190万分钟。托尼·罗宾斯推出的人生导师聊天机器人收费更高，月费达99美元——但新用户可享受前14天0.99美元的体验价。而灵性导师大卫·吉亚姆提供了浮动定价方案，用户每月仅需1美元即可与他的人工智能分身交流，比起他每小时高达1.5万美元的一对一私教费用，这显然实惠得多。

paragraphs.contentEn: Whether any of these tools actually work for the people paying for the services, you’d have to ask them. Self-help can have its place, though the industry is undoubtedly filled with bunk research and bad advice. But one thing is for sure: It’s working great for the gurus. Hussey told the Wall Street Journal, “I literally can’t do what it is doing,” which is true in the sense that he can’t speak to people at the scale that his chatbot can. But it’s also literally not doing what he is doing. Whatever you may think of the validity of a dating coach, the selling point is getting personalized advice based on your situation and their experience. A chatbot simulates that, sure, but it actually doesn’t know anything about you, your relationship, or relationships broadly. It is a chatbot. It can sound like Hussey and recreate Hussey’s words, but it doesn’t know what any of them mean.
paragraphs.contentZh: 对于付费使用者而言，这些工具是否真的有效，恐怕只能由当事人自己来评判。自助类内容或许有其存在价值，但这一行业确实充斥着缺乏依据的研究和误导性的建议。不过，有一点可以确定：对那些导师本人而言，效果相当显著。赫西接受《华尔街日报》采访时表示：“我确实做不到它正在做的事情”，某种意义上这话没错，他确实无法像自己的聊天机器人那样，同时与这么多人进行互动。但从实质来看，这个机器人其实也并没有在做他真正所做的事。无论人们如何评价情感导师这一职业，其核心卖点始终在于基于当事人的具体处境，并结合自身经验，提供有针对性的个人建议。聊天机器人确实可以模拟这种形式，但它并不了解你、你的关系，甚至也不了解亲密关系本身。它只是一个聊天机器人。它可以模仿赫西的语气，复现他的表述，却并不理解这些话究竟意味着什么。

paragraphs.contentEn: Gabby Bernstein, a spiritual teacher who has come under fire in the past for pseudo-scientific claims, charges $199 a year for her Gabby AI, made the case that the chatbot is effectively offering herself to the world. “It’s backed with 20 years of books, lectures, workshops and meditations. So it’s me, it’s my message, and only I could control that,” she told WSJ. Though, notably, she doesn’t control that. She’s turned it over to Delphi AI, a venture capital-backed startup that has created an entire micro-industry out of selling self-help AI as a service.
paragraphs.contentZh: 灵性导师加比·伯恩斯坦曾因伪科学主张引发争议，如今也推出了年费199美元的个人人工智能分身“Gabby AI”，并声称这款产品相当于将我自己呈现给全世界。她在接受《华尔街日报》采访时表示：“这个聊天机器人融汇了我过去二十年的全部著作、演讲、工作坊内容以及冥想体悟。所以它就是我，传达的是我的信息，并且只有我能掌控这一切。”但值得注意的是，她实际并未控制该产品。这款聊天机器人已交由风险投资支持的初创公司Delphi AI运营，该公司已将自助型人工智能服务发展为一个成熟的微型产业。

paragraphs.contentEn: Bernstein does perhaps sum up the whole situation best, albeit likely by accident. “If I don’t do it, someone else is going to do it in a way that’s not in alignment with my truth,” she told WSJ. You could simplify that to “If I don’t do it, someone else is going to get these people’s money,” and it wouldn’t fundamentally change the meaning. Need proof? Tony Robbins sued a company that made a chatbot using his likeness, then turned around and launched his own.
paragraphs.contentZh: 尽管很可能出于无意，但伯恩斯坦的话或许最精准地概括了当前的局面。她告诉《华尔街日报》：“如果我不去做这件事，其他人就会以一种不符合我理念的方式去做。”这一说法完全可以简化为：“如果我不赚这份钱，别人就会赚走这些人的钱”，两者的核心意思并无本质区别。还需要更多证明？托尼・罗宾斯曾起诉一家未经许可使用其形象开发聊天机器人的公司，但不久后，他自己也推出了类似的产品。
